evidence.statement: The exact inventoried passive source defines 22 powered loadout IDs over 15 passive families. Storm Generator stores Damage 1/2 for base/A, Viscera Nanobots stores Heal 1/2, Networked Armor stores Health 1/2, and Vek Hormones stores Damage 1/2/2/3 for base/A/B/AB; every constructor supplies the native Passive string that distinguishes its effective variant.

The Advanced Edition Skill_Repair override removes Fire, ACID, and Injured, then repeats the same SpaceDamage over every other TEAM_MECH pawn when Mass_Repair is active. The shipped descriptions state that Repair Field affects all Mechs, Auto-Shields shields a building after damage, Stabilizers prevents emerging-Vek damage to Mechs, and the remaining passive families have the named global effects.

The ten passive GetSkillEffect callbacks operate on fixed TipImage coordinates and demonstrate presentation examples; ordinary combat behavior is therefore a native engine dependency keyed by each constructor's Passive string, rather than an action emitted by those callbacks.

Simulator v379 preserves exact Storm Generator and Vek Hormones upgrade magnitudes and adds bounded Repair Field, Auto-Shields, and Stabilizers board effects. Source-catalogued passive IDs remain outside Rust WId action slots while save overlays preserve their exact powered variants.

The exact Advanced Edition source defines Nanofilter Mending, Heat Engines, Networked Shielding, and Void Shocker as four base-only PassiveSkill constructors. Their callbacks are fixed TipImage demonstrations; the shipped English localization states the native board contracts for smoke healing, fire-to-Boost conversion, player-turn mech damage immunity, and one Void Shocker damage after a Vek attack damages no unit or building.

VoidShockImmune defaults false on pawn definitions and is true on source-defined support/spawner families including Blobbers, Shamans, Spiders/eggs, and Psions. Simulator v380 imports that exact pawn property, models Networked Shielding only through the player-phase boundary, and evaluates Void Shocker after each complete queued attack using actual unit/building HP loss.

Passive_VoidShock has no Upgrades, UpgradeCost, UpgradeList, or Damage field and therefore inherits Skill.Upgrades=0. The executable and local save corpus contain no Passive_VoidShock_A runtime ID; the localization-only +1 Damage strings are orphan text and are deliberately excluded from catalogs and save overlays.

known_gaps: Psionic Receiver aura acquisition/application, Ammo Generator cross-turn limited-use accounting, and Critical Shields' one-shot grid-threshold history remain native engine dependencies without controlled build-keyed traces.

Forestry Nano is removed from ordinary drops in this build and its death-to-Forest behavior is not simulated. Viscera Nanobots, Flame Shielding, Force Amp, and Medical Supplies retain their earlier bounded implementations but do not have exhaustive native scheduler/status conformance.

Networked Armor and Kickoff Boosters are trusted through live effective HP and Move values; Rust does not independently reproduce their native mission-start or turn-start application and adjacency timing.

Auto-Shields is implemented after known Rust building-damage paths, but native trigger ordering across every SpaceDamage, grid-resist, multi-effect, destruction, and mission-script edge has not been captured independently.

Networked Shielding protects numeric damage routed through the simulator's shared player-phase damage core and Old Earth Mine DAMAGE_DEATH paths. Native treatment of non-damage instant-death terrain and unusual mission-script direct HP mutation remains untraced.

Void Shocker uses per-attack unit/building HP loss and the bridged VoidShockImmune property. Native ordering against net-zero damage-plus-heal actions, mission-script mutations, Armor/ACID on the retaliated Vek, and death-effect chains remains without a controlled trace.
The passive callback bodies prove tooltip examples and fields, not the native Passive-string implementation. No fresh controlled capture was taken during the protected live achievement session.

evidence.statement: The exact inventoried Cataclysm environment advances one column per Plan call, marks every non-building tile in that column, permanently blocks the adjacent future column from spawning, and applies TERRAIN_HOLE to every marked tile. Its mission lasts three turns.

The exact inventoried Seismic environment builds one native random cross path, then selects up to three consecutive path cells per Plan call, permanently blocks those cells from spawning, and applies TERRAIN_HOLE. Its inherited target predicate excludes invalid, pod, and building tiles but permits Water.

The exact inventoried Lightning environment chooses one valid tile from each of four interior 3-by-3 quarters. Each selected tile receives DAMAGE_DEATH without a terrain override; the inherited validity predicate excludes invalid, pod, building, and Water tiles.

Simulator v382 converts bridge-selected Cataclysm and Seismic non-building danger tiles to Chasm while preserving the established flyer-immunity distinction, leaves Lightning terrain unchanged while killing flyers, and consumes resolved non-Tides danger markers in projected and replayed boards instead of firing the same current warning again.

known_gaps: Rust consumes the bridge-selected current danger mask. It does not serialize or reproduce Cataclysm Index, Seismic Path or Index, Lightning/Seismic Locations, Planned, or CurrentAttack, native random_int/random_element/random_removal calls, candidate order, or RNG state.

Projected and replayed boards consume a resolved non-Tides danger mask but cannot construct the next native Cataclysm, Lightning, or Seismic warning. Clearing the old mask is exact non-repetition, not a claim that future missions have no environment event.

Rust scans the live bitset in tile-index order. Native unordered Lightning locations resolve by random removal, ordered Seismic locations resolve serially, and Cataclysm applies a source-built column; death chains and other order-sensitive interactions are not exhaustively conformant.

Native temporary and permanent spawn-block source state is not serialized for these missions. Cataclysm's future-column block, Seismic's selected-path blocks, Lightning's inherited temporary blocks, and their interaction with emergence remain live-engine dependencies.
